paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The average probing accuracy using different MLP variations. We indicate the size(s) of hidden layer(s) in square brackets.
model_annotation: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the percentage point difference in probing accuracy across various multi-layer perceptron (MLP) variations. The horizontal axis contains the categories, displaying four distinct MLP configurations ordered from left to right: "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU", with no explicit axis label and no specific alphabetical or value-based sorting. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "% point difference," using a linear scale that ranges from -0.2 to 0.2. This axis features numeric tick labels at intervals of 0.1, with corresponding horizontal grid lines spanning the width of the chart, including a solid gray line marking the 0.0 baseline. Within each category on the horizontal axis, the chart features two adjacent vertical bars representing different language models, as defined by a legend in the top right corner. The light blue bars represent the "mBERT" model, while the dark blue bars represent the "XLM-R" model, and all bars are visually emphasized with solid black outlines. For the "hidden:[50], linear" category, the mBERT bar reaches approximately -0.20 (the lowest negative value on the chart), while the XLM-R bar is around -0.06. In the "hidden:[], linear" category, both bars extend upward, with mBERT at approximately 0.09 and XLM-R reaching the chart's maximum positive value at roughly 0.21. For "hidden:[100], ReLU", the mBERT bar extends downward to roughly -0.12, while the XLM-R bar points slightly upward to approximately 0.03. Finally, in the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" category, both bars extend downward, with mBERT at nearly -0.18 and XLM-R at approximately -0.14.
